subject: Agriculture
title: Milking Machines and Dairy Tech
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Milking Machines and Dairy Tech.

hook.text: A robotic milking system lets cows choose when to be milked. No farmer required. The cow walks in voluntarily.

buildup.text: Hand-milking was the bottleneck of dairy farming—each cow took 10 minutes, twice daily, 365 days a year.

discovery.text: The first practical milking machine arrived in 1894. Modern rotary parlors can milk 100 cows per hour.

twist.text: Robotic milking systems cost $200,000 each—but they milk 24/7, analyze milk quality, and detect mastitis early.

climax.text: Cows milked by robots produce 5–10% more milk. Less stress, more frequent milking, and individual attention.

punchline.text: The cow decides when to be milked. The robot does the rest. The farmer sleeps.

quiz.question: What extra benefit do robotic milking systems provide cows?
options: Cows produce 5–10% more milk due to less stress and more frequent milking
